mn108:1.2: On one occasion the venerable Ānanda was living at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place, not long after the Blessed One had attained final Nibbāna.
mn108:2.1: Now on that occasion Ajātasattu Vedehiputta, King of Magadha, was having Rājagaha fortified, being suspicious of King Pajjota.
mn108:3.1: Then, when it was morning, the venerable Ānanda dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he went into Rājagaha for alms.
mn108:3.2: Then it occurred to the venerable Ānanda:
mn108:3.3: “It is still too early to wander for alms in Rājagaha.
mn108:3.4: What if I went to where the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna is at work, to see the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna?”
mn108:4.1: Then the venerable Ānanda went to where the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna was at work, to the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna.
mn108:4.2: The brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna saw the venerable Ānanda coming in the distance.
mn108:4.3: On seeing him, he said to the venerable Ānanda:
mn108:4.6: It is long since Master Ānanda found the opportunity to come here.
mn108:4.7: Let Master Ānanda be seated; this seat is ready.”
mn108:4.8: The venerable Ānanda sat down on the seat made ready.
mn108:4.9: The brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna took a certain low seat and sat down at one side.
mn108:4.10: When he had done so, the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna said to the venerable Ānanda:
mn108:5.1: “Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu who possesses in every way and in every part those dhammas that Master Gotama, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, possessed?”
mn108:5.2: “There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, who possesses in every way and in every part those dhammas that the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, possessed.
mn108:5.3: For, brahmin, the Blessed One was the arouser of the path unarisen, the producer of the path unproduced, the declarer of the path undeclared; he was the knower of the path, the finder of the path, one skilled in the path;
mn108:5.4: but his disciples now abide following the path, and become possessed of it afterwards.”[^1]
mn108:6.1: Now this conversation between the venerable Ānanda and the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna was left unfinished.
mn108:6.2: For then the brahmin Vassakāra, the Magadhan chief minister, who was supervising the works at Rājagaha, went to where the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna was at work, to the venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.
mn108:6.3: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the brahmin Vassakāra, the Magadhan chief minister, said to the venerable Ānanda:
mn108:6.4: “For what talk, Master Ānanda, are you sitting together now, and what was your conversation that was left unfinished?”
mn108:6.5: “Here, brahmin, the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna said this to me:
mn108:6.6: ‘Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu who possesses in every way and in every part those dhammas that Master Gotama possessed?’
mn108:6.7: When this was said, brahmin, I said this to the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna:
mn108:6.8: ‘There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, who possesses in every way and in every part those dhammas that the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, possessed.[^2]
mn108:6.9: For, brahmin, the Blessed One was the arouser of the path unarisen, the producer of the path unproduced, the declarer of the path undeclared; he was the knower of the path, the finder of the path, one skilled in the path;
mn108:6.10: but his disciples now abide following the path, and become possessed of it afterwards.’
mn108:6.11: This, brahmin, is the conversation between me and the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna that was left unfinished.
mn108:7.1: “Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu appointed by Master Gotama thus:
mn108:7.2: ‘This one will be your refuge when I am gone’, on whom you might now depend?”
mn108:7.3: “There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, appointed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, thus:
mn108:7.4: ‘This one will be your refuge when I am gone’, on whom we might now depend.”[^3]
mn108:8.1: “But, Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu agreed upon by the Saṅgha and appointed by a number of elder bhikkhus thus:
mn108:8.2: ‘This one will be our refuge after the Blessed One is gone’, on whom you might now depend?”
mn108:8.3: “There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, agreed upon by the Saṅgha and appointed by a number of elder bhikkhus thus:
mn108:8.4: ‘This one will be our refuge after the Blessed One is gone’, on whom we might now depend.”
mn108:9.1: “But, Master Ānanda, if you are thus without refuge, what is the reason for your concord?”
mn108:9.4: we have the Dhamma as our refuge.”
mn108:10.1: “‘Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu appointed by Master Gotama thus—
mn108:10.2: “This one will be your refuge when I am gone”, on whom you might now depend?’—
mn108:10.3: when asked thus, you say: ‘There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, appointed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, thus—
mn108:10.4: “This one will be your refuge when I am gone”, on whom we might now depend’;
mn108:10.5: ‘But, Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu agreed upon by the Saṅgha and appointed by a number of elder bhikkhus thus—
mn108:10.6: “This one will be our refuge after the Blessed One is gone”, on whom you might now depend?’—
mn108:10.7: when asked thus, you say: ‘There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, agreed upon by the Saṅgha and appointed by a number of elder bhikkhus thus—
mn108:10.8: “This one will be our refuge after the Blessed One is gone”, on whom we might now depend’—
mn108:10.10: ‘But, Master Ānanda, if you are thus without refuge, what is the reason for your concord?’—when asked thus, you say: ‘We are not without refuge, brahmin;
mn108:10.12: we have the Dhamma as our refuge’—so you say.
mn108:10.13: Now, Master Ānanda, how should the meaning of this statement be regarded?”
mn108:10.14: “There is, brahmin, a training precept laid down for the bhikkhus by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One; the Pātimokkha has been recited.
mn108:10.15: As many of us as live in dependence on one village district assemble together on that day for the Uposatha.
mn108:10.16: Having assembled, we invite whoever knows the recitation to recite it.
mn108:10.17: If, while it is being recited, there is an offence, a transgression, in the case of a bhikkhu, we make him act[^4] according to the Dhamma, according to the instruction that has been given.
mn108:10.18: It is not, indeed, that the venerable ones make us act;
mn108:10.19: it is the Dhamma that makes us act.”
mn108:11.1: “Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu whom you now honour, respect, revere and venerate, and, honouring and respecting him, live in dependence on?”
mn108:11.2: “There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, whom we now honour, respect, revere and venerate, and, honouring and respecting him, live in dependence on.”
mn108:11.3: “‘Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu appointed by Master Gotama thus—
mn108:11.4: “This one will be your refuge when I am gone”, on whom you might now depend?’—
mn108:11.5: when asked thus, you say: ‘There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, appointed by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, thus—
mn108:12.1: “This one will be your refuge when I am gone”, on whom we might now depend’;
mn108:12.2: ‘But, Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu agreed upon by the Saṅgha and appointed by a number of elder bhikkhus thus—
mn108:12.3: “This one will be our refuge after the Blessed One is gone”, on whom you might now depend?’—
mn108:12.4: when asked thus, you say: ‘There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, agreed upon by the Saṅgha and appointed by a number of elder bhikkhus thus—
mn108:12.5: “This one will be our refuge after the Blessed One is gone”, on whom we might now depend’;
mn108:12.6: ‘Master Ānanda, is there any single bhikkhu whom you now honour, respect, revere and venerate, and, honouring and respecting him, live in dependence on?’—
mn108:12.7: when asked thus, you say: ‘There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, whom we now honour, respect, revere and venerate, and, honouring and respecting him, live in dependence on’—so you say.
mn108:12.8: Now, Master Ānanda, how should the meaning of this statement be regarded?”
mn108:13.1: “There are, brahmin, ten dhammas that inspire confidence, declared by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One.
mn108:13.2: In whomever among us these dhammas are found, him we now honour, respect, revere and venerate, and, honouring and respecting him, we live in dependence on him.
mn108:14.1: Here, brahmin, a bhikkhu is virtuous, he dwells restrained with the restraint of the Pātimokkha, perfect in conduct and resort, and, seeing danger in the slightest fault, trains himself by undertaking the training precepts.
mn108:15.1: He has learnt much, remembers what he has learnt, and consolidates what he has learnt.
mn108:15.2: Those dhammas that are good in the beginning, good in the middle and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, that proclaim the life divine that is utterly perfect and pure—such dhammas as those he has learnt much of, remembered, consolidated by recitation,[^5] examined with the mind, and penetrated well by view.
mn108:16.1: He is content with robes, almsfood, resting place, and the requisite of medicine for the sick.
mn108:17.1: He is one who obtains at will, without trouble or difficulty, the four jhānas that pertain to the higher mind and provide a pleasant abiding here and now.
mn108:18.1: He wields the various kinds of supernormal power: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one; he appears and vanishes; he goes unhindered through a wall, through a rampart, through a mountain, as though through space; he dives in and out of the earth as though it were water; he walks on water without sinking as though on earth; seated cross-legged, he travels through the air like a bird on the wing; with his hand he touches and strokes the moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; he wields bodily mastery even as far as the Brahmā world.
mn108:19.1: He hears, with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, both kinds of sounds, the divine and the human, those that are far as well as near.
mn108:20.1: Having encompassed the minds of other beings and other persons with his own mind, he understands them—
mn108:20.2: he understands a mind with lust as a mind with lust,
mn108:20.3: and a mind without lust as a mind without lust;
mn108:20.4: he understands a mind with hate as a mind with hate,
mn108:20.5: and a mind without hate as a mind without hate;
mn108:20.6: he understands a mind with delusion as a mind with delusion,
mn108:20.7: and a mind without delusion as a mind without delusion;
mn108:20.8: he understands a contracted mind as contracted,
mn108:20.9: and a distracted mind as distracted;
mn108:20.10: he understands an exalted mind as exalted,
mn108:20.11: and an unexalted mind as unexalted;
mn108:20.12: he understands a surpassable mind as surpassable,
mn108:20.13: and an unsurpassable mind as unsurpassable;
mn108:20.14: he understands a concentrated mind as concentrated,
mn108:20.15: and an unconcentrated mind as unconcentrated;
mn108:20.16: he understands a liberated mind as liberated,
mn108:20.17: and an unliberated mind as unliberated.
mn108:21.1: He recollects his manifold past lives, that is to say, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births, many aeons of world contraction, many aeons of world expansion, many aeons of world contraction and expansion: ‘There he was so named, of such a race, with such appearance, such was his nutriment, such his experience of pleasure and pain, such his life-term; and passing away from there, he appeared elsewhere; and there too he was so named, of such a race, with such appearance, such was his nutriment, such his experience of pleasure and pain, such his life-term; and passing away from there, he appeared here.’ Thus with details and particulars he recollects his manifold past lives.
mn108:22.1: With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, fair and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and he understands how beings pass on according to their actions.
mn108:23.1: By realizing for himself with direct knowledge, he here and now enters upon and abides in the deliverance of mind and the deliverance by wisdom that are taintless with the exhaustion of the taints.
mn108:23.2: These, brahmin, are the ten dhammas that inspire confidence, declared by the Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One.
mn108:23.3: In whomever among us these dhammas are found, him we now honour, respect, revere and venerate, and, honouring and respecting him, we live in dependence on him.”
mn108:24.1: When this was said, the brahmin Vassakāra, the Magadhan chief minister, said to General Upananda:
mn108:24.2: “What do you think, General? If these venerable ones honour him who should be honoured, respect him who should be respected,
mn108:24.3: revere him who should be revered, and venerate him who should be venerated—
mn108:24.4: then indeed these venerable ones honour him who should be honoured, respect him who should be respected, revere him who should be revered, and venerate him who should be venerated.
mn108:24.5: For if these venerable ones did not honour, respect, revere and venerate this one,
mn108:24.6: then whom indeed would these venerable ones honour, respect, revere and venerate, and, honouring, respecting, revering and venerating him, live in dependence on?”
mn108:25.1: Then the brahmin Vassakāra, the Magadhan chief minister, said to the venerable Ānanda:
mn108:25.2: “And where does Master Ānanda now live?”
mn108:25.3: “I now live in the Bamboo Grove, brahmin.”
mn108:25.4: “I hope, Master Ānanda, that the Bamboo Grove is delightful, quiet, undisturbed by noise, secluded from people, remote from crowds, favourable for retreat?”
mn108:25.5: “Indeed, brahmin, the Bamboo Grove is delightful, quiet, undisturbed by noise, secluded from people, remote from crowds, favourable for retreat, thanks to such guardians and protectors as yourself.”
mn108:25.6: “Indeed, Master Ānanda, the Bamboo Grove is delightful, quiet, undisturbed by noise, secluded from people, remote from crowds, favourable for retreat, thanks to such venerable ones as you, who meditate and are devoted to meditation.
mn108:25.7: For the venerable ones do meditate, and are devoted to meditation.
mn108:25.8: Once, Master Ānanda, on one occasion Master Gotama was living at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.
mn108:25.9: Then I went to the Great Wood, to the Hall with the Peaked Roof, to Master Gotama.
mn108:25.10: And there Master Gotama spoke on the subject of jhāna in many ways.
mn108:25.11: Master Gotama was indeed one who meditated and was devoted to meditation,
mn108:25.12: and Master Gotama commended all sorts of jhāna.”
mn108:26.1: “It is not, brahmin, that the Blessed One commended all sorts of jhāna, nor is it that he did not commend all sorts of jhāna.
mn108:26.2: What sort of jhāna, brahmin, did the Blessed One not commend?
mn108:26.3: Here, brahmin, someone abides with his mind obsessed by sensual lust, a prey to sensual lust, and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from sensual lust once it has arisen;
mn108:26.4: making that sensual lust the main thing,[^6] he meditates on it, meditates about it, meditates because of it, meditates over it.
mn108:26.5: He abides with his mind obsessed by ill will, a prey to ill will, and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from ill will once it has arisen;
mn108:26.6: making that ill will the main thing, he meditates on it, meditates about it, meditates because of it, meditates over it.
mn108:26.7: He abides with his mind obsessed by lethargy and drowsiness, a prey to lethargy and drowsiness, and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from lethargy and drowsiness once it has arisen;
mn108:26.8: making that lethargy and drowsiness the main thing, he meditates on it, meditates about it, meditates because of it, meditates over it.
mn108:26.9: He abides with his mind obsessed by agitation and worry, a prey to agitation and worry, and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from agitation and worry once it has arisen;
mn108:26.10: making that agitation and worry the main thing, he meditates on it, meditates about it, meditates because of it, meditates over it.
mn108:26.11: He abides with his mind obsessed by uncertainty, a prey to uncertainty, and he does not understand as it actually is the escape from uncertainty once it has arisen;
mn108:26.12: making that uncertainty the main thing, he meditates on it, meditates about it, meditates because of it, meditates over it.
mn108:26.13: Such is the sort of jhāna, brahmin, that the Blessed One did not commend.[^7]
mn108:27.1: What sort of jhāna, brahmin, did the Blessed One commend?
mn108:27.2: Here, brahmin, quite secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unprofitable dhammas, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained application, with happiness and pleasure born of seclusion.
mn108:27.3: With the stilling of initial and sustained application, he enters upon and abides in the second jhāna …
mn108:27.5: he enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
mn108:27.6: Such is the sort of jhāna, brahmin, that the Blessed One commended.”
mn108:28.1: “It seems, Master Ānanda, that Master Gotama censured the sort of jhāna that should be censured, and praised the sort of jhāna that should be praised.
mn108:28.2: But now, Master Ānanda, we must go;
mn108:28.3: we are busy and have much to do.”
mn108:28.4: “Now, brahmin, is the time for you to do as you see fit.”
mn108:28.5: Then the brahmin Vassakāra, the Magadhan chief minister, having delighted in and approved of the venerable Ānanda’s words, rose from his seat and departed.
mn108:29.1: Then, soon after the brahmin Vassakāra, the Magadhan chief minister, had left, the brahmin Gopaka Moggallāna said to the venerable Ānanda:
mn108:29.2: “What we asked Master Ānanda, Master Ānanda has not answered.”
mn108:29.4: ‘There is no single bhikkhu, brahmin, who possesses in every way and in every part those dhammas that the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Fully Enlightened One, possessed.
mn108:29.5: For, brahmin, the Blessed One was the arouser of the path unarisen, the producer of the path unproduced, the declarer of the path undeclared; he was the knower of the path, the finder of the path, one skilled in the path.
mn108:29.6: But his disciples now abide following the path, and become possessed of it afterwards’?”
